Elena —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Attaching the updated quote and a rolling schedule (Perpetua_Rolling_Schedule_v3.xlsx) that maps expected usage and token tiers over the next 24 months. High level:

- Option A (annual prepay, 2yr): Year 1 prepaid for 100% of forecasted usage, Year 2 prepaid with a 10% rollover buffer.
- Option B (annual, split): Annual prepay with the option to split payment 60/40 across two invoices per year.

I put together both payment rhythms because you mentioned procurement prefers annual commitments but finance may need split invoices. The attached PDF includes line-item pricing and a standard 12% term discount for a 2-year commit.

Could you confirm which payment rhythm Perpetua prefers (Option A vs B) and whether procurement needs a different billing cadence? If you want us to price a steeper term discount or a custom ramp, say so and I’ll pull the numbers.

Attaching: redwood_quote_2026-08-15.pdf, Perpetua_Rolling_Schedule_v3.xlsx

Thanks Jordan — helpful summary and attachments. A couple of notes from procurement/finance:

- Procurement prefers an annual prepay for accounting simplicity, but they need an option to rollover unused credits up to 15% into year 2.
- Finance has asked if we can structure the payment as annual prepay but allow split invoicing (two invoices per year) for cashflow reasons.
- On discount: our head of platform is asking if Redwood can improve the term discount to 16–18% on Year 1 given the ARR size (we're targeting a 24-month commitment at ~1.2M ARR).

Can you confirm whether Redwood can offer a 2-year annual prepay with a 15% rollover cap and an enhanced Year 1 discount (target 18%)? If you need to route for approvals, please let me know timeline — procurement needs a signed amendment by end of month to align with our quarter close.

Jordan — thanks for the heads-up. Some quick math and risk points:

- Baseline (12% standard 2yr term discount) gives acceptable unit economics for the quoted load. An 18% Year 1 discount would reduce blended margin substantially unless offset by onboarding fee or usage floor.
- Alternative we can approve at deal desk: 15% Year 1, 10% Year 2, with a 15% rollover cap and a 3-month minimum ramp (i.e., minimum committed consumption to avoid excessive churn risk). Also recommend a $25k onboarding credit to sweeten the commercial terms.
- If Sales wants to push to 18% Year 1, we'll need VP approval (represents an exception to current pricing bands).

If Perpetua is signing by 8/31, we can move fast. Please prepare the amendment text and call out the ramp minimum.

-Markus
VP Revenue Operations
markus.klein@redwood.ai
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>

Date: Sun, 16 Aug 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Requesting final approval for Perpetua 2yr amendment (15/10 + $25k onboarding)

Vivek — Perpetua (Elena) is requesting 18% Year 1. Markus recommends 15% Y1 / 10% Y2 + $25k onboarding credit and 15% rollover cap, plus a 3-month minimum ramp. They need a signed amendment by 8/31.

Summary of proposed final commercial package for approval:
- Term: 24 months (annual prepay each year)
- Pricing: Year 1 = list minus 15%, Year 2 = list minus 10%
- Rollover: unused credits can roll into Year 2 up to 15% of Year 1 purchased units
- Ramp: 3-month minimum committed ramp (floor) to protect unit economics
- Onboarding: $25,000 credit applied to first invoice
- Payment: annual prepay, with optional split invoicing (two invoices) upon request

If you approve, I'll get Legal to prepare the amendment and send DocuSign to Perpetua today.

Thanks — Jordan
